subQuestions.questionText:
Match the concept BMI (body mass index) with the correct explanation/definition (A to J) from TABLE 1.

TABLE 1: EXPLANATIONS AND DEFINITIONS OF CONCEPTS
A - The distance from the centre of a circle to the outer part of the circle
B - The use of cardinal directions (i.e. north, south, east and west) to describe the location of one point to the other
C - The path or boundary that surrounds a circular-shaped object or surface
D - A position which is not exact, but roughly shows the location of an object
E - A measure of body fat based on the height and weight of an adult person
F - The total area of all the faces of a 3D-shaped object
G - A special type of diagram used to determine the outcomes of an event in probability examples
H - The arrangement of something laid out, such as the structural features of a mall
I - The ratio of the distance in real life compared to the same distance on a map
J - The rate of covering a certain distance over time
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identifying letter E ✓
Mark 2: Correct match with BMI ✓
Answer: E (A measure of body fat based on the height and weight of an adult person)

subQuestions.questionText:
The pedestal is shaped like a cylinder with a diameter of 124 mm and a height of 124 mm.

Choose a formula (A, B or C) below which can be used to calculate the total volume of the pedestal.

NOTE: In EACH formula, $r$ = radius and $h$ = height.

A. $\text{Volume} = (2 \times \pi \times r \times h) + (2 \times \pi \times r^2)$
B. $\text{Volume} = (2 \times \pi \times r^2) \times h$
C. $\text{Volume} = \pi \times r^2 \times h$
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identifying correct formula letter ✓
Mark 2: Correct formula for volume of cylinder ✓

Answer: C — $\text{Volume} = \pi \times r^2 \times h$

Reason: The volume of a cylinder is calculated as the area of the circular base ($\pi r^2$) multiplied by the height. Formula A is for surface area, and formula B is incorrect (extra factor of 2).

options.A: Volume = (2 × π × r × h) + (2 × π × r²)

subQuestions.questionText: Write down the unit of measurement for the volume of the pedestal using the given unit in the diagram. (Diameter = 124 mm, Height = 124 mm.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identifying that the unit on the diagram is mm ✓
Mark 2: Correctly cubing the unit for volume ✓

Answer: $mm^3$ (cubic millimetres)

Explanation: Since dimensions are given in mm and volume is a 3D measurement, the unit is mm cubed.

subQuestions.questionText: Convert the height of the pedestal (124 mm) to metres.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Correct conversion factor (1 m = 1000 mm) ✓
Mark 2: Correct final answer with unit ✓

Calculation: $124 \text{ mm} \div 1000 = 0,124 \text{ m}$

Answer: $0,124$ m

subQuestions.questionText: The scale used on a wall map in a classroom is 1 : 250 000. Use the given scale to determine the distance on the wall map if the real distance is 65 kilometres.

$\text{Map distance} = 6\,500\,000 \div 250\,000 = 26 \text{ cm}$

subQuestions.questionText:
A Mathematical Literacy teacher collected 36 reams of paper from her learners. The dimensions of a ream of paper are: Length (L) = 27,94 cm, Width (W) = 21,59 cm, Height (H) = 6,35 cm. The dimensions of the maximum space on one shelf of a cabinet are 102 cm long, 44 cm wide and 39 cm high.

Show, with calculations, that all the reams of paper collected can fit on ONE shelf of the cabinet.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Number of reams along length: $102 \div 27,94 = 3,65... \approx 3$ reams ✓
Mark 2: Number of reams along width: $44 \div 21,59 = 2,03... \approx 2$ reams ✓
Mark 3: Number of reams stacked in height: $39 \div 6,35 = 6,14... \approx 6$ reams ✓
Mark 4: Multiplying to get total: $3 \times 2 \times 6$ ✓
Mark 5: Total = 36 reams ✓
Mark 6: Comparing 36 to 36 ✓
Mark 7: Conclusion that all 36 reams fit on one shelf ✓

Calculation:
Along length: $102 \div 27,94 \approx 3$ reams (rounded down)
Along width: $44 \div 21,59 \approx 2$ reams (rounded down)
Stacked: $39 \div 6,35 \approx 6$ reams (rounded down)
Total capacity: $3 \times 2 \times 6 = 36$ reams

Conclusion: Since the shelf can hold exactly 36 reams and the teacher has 36 reams, all reams can fit on ONE shelf. ✓

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why the teacher would like to pack the reams of paper in the cabinet.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Valid reason ✓
Mark 2: Reason linked to cabinet/security ✓

Acceptable answers (any ONE):
- The cabinet is secure / lockable, preventing theft
- To protect the paper from damage (e.g. moisture, dust)
- To keep the paper organised / neatly stored
- To prevent unauthorised access by learners
- To keep paper in good condition for examinations/printing

[Any reasonable answer linked to security, protection, or organisation is accepted.]

questions.title: Plastering Walls, Probability, and Mixing Plaster

subQuestions.questionText:
Unathi bought a house. Two of the walls in one of the bedrooms were not plastered. The dimensions of the floor of this bedroom are 4,8 m × 3,5 m, with a wall height of 2,75 m.

Calculate, in $m^2$, the total surface area of the two walls that need to be plastered.

You may use the following formula: Area of a rectangle = length × width
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Area of wall 1: $4,8 \times 2,75$ ✓
Mark 2: Area of wall 1 = $13,2$ $m^2$ ✓
Mark 3: Area of wall 2: $3,5 \times 2,75 = 9,625$ $m^2$ ✓
Mark 4: Total area: $13,2 + 9,625 = 22,825$ $m^2$ ✓

Calculation:
Wall 1 area = $4,8 \times 2,75 = 13,2$ $m^2$
Wall 2 area = $3,5 \times 2,75 = 9,625$ $m^2$
Total surface area = $13,2 + 9,625 = 22,825$ $m^2$

Answer: $22,825$ $m^2$

subQuestions.questionText:
The plaster on the walls has a uniform thickness of 12 mm. Determine, in $cm^3$, the volume of plaster required to plaster these two walls.

You may use the following formula: Volume of plaster = area of walls × thickness of plaster
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Converting area to $cm^2$: $22,825 \text{ m}^2 = 228\,250 \text{ cm}^2$ ✓
Mark 2: Converting thickness to cm: $12 \text{ mm} = 1,2 \text{ cm}$ ✓
Mark 3: Substitution into formula ✓
Mark 4: Calculation: $228\,250 \times 1,2$ ✓
Mark 5: Final answer with unit: $273\,900$ $cm^3$ ✓

Calculation:
Area = $22,825$ $m^2$ = $22,825 \times 10\,000 = 228\,250$ $cm^2$
Thickness = $12$ mm = $1,2$ cm
Volume = $228\,250 \times 1,2 = 273\,900$ $cm^3$

Answer: $273\,900$ $cm^3$

subQuestions.questionText: The ready-mix plaster is available in bags. One bag is needed for every 15 000 $cm^3$. Determine the minimum number of bags needed to plaster the two walls.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Dividing volume by bag capacity: $273\,900 \div 15\,000$ ✓
Mark 2: Result = $18,26$ ✓
Mark 3: Rounding up to 19 bags ✓

Calculation:
$273\,900 \div 15\,000 = 18,26$
Since a partial bag must be rounded UP (you cannot buy 0,26 of a bag and you need enough plaster), the minimum number of bags = 19.

Answer: $19$ bags

subQuestions.questionText:
Unathi would also like to have all the old cornices in the bedroom, where the four walls meet the ceiling, replaced. Calculate, in metres, the total length of the new cornices.

You may use the following formula: Perimeter = 2 × (length + width)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Substitution into perimeter formula: $2 \times (4,8 + 3,5)$ ✓
Mark 2: Calculation: $2 \times 8,3$ ✓
Mark 3: Final answer with unit: $16,6$ m ✓

Calculation:
Perimeter = $2 \times (\text{length} + \text{width})$
            = $2 \times (4,8 + 3,5)$
            = $2 \times 8,3$
            = $16,6$ m

Answer: $16,6$ m

subQuestions.questionText: Unathi is advised to choose a specific brand of ready-mix plaster to prevent dampness in the walls. At the store, there are five available brands. Unfortunately, Unathi forgets the name of the specific brand. If she randomly selects one of the available brands, determine the probability that she will select the specific brand.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identifying favourable outcomes (1) and total outcomes (5) ✓
Mark 2: Correct probability ✓

Calculation:
$P(\text{specific brand}) = \dfrac{1}{5} = 0,2 = 20\%$

Answer: $\dfrac{1}{5}$ OR $0,2$ OR $20\%$

subQuestions.questionText: There is a 0,75 probability that the dampness will appear if the incorrect brand of ready-mix plaster is used. Determine the probability that the dampness will NOT appear if the incorrect ready-mix plaster is used.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Recognising complementary probability: $1 - 0,75$ ✓
Mark 2: Final answer ✓

Calculation:
$P(\text{not damp}) = 1 - 0,75 = 0,25$

Answer: $0,25$ OR $\dfrac{1}{4}$ OR $25\%$

subQuestions.questionText:
The probability scale shows the likelihoods for various probabilities (not possible, less likely, equally likely, more likely, certain — from 0% to 100%).

Write down the likelihood that best describes your answer given to QUESTION 3.2.2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Linking 0,25 (25%) to a position on the scale ✓
Mark 2: Correct likelihood term ✓

Answer: Less likely

Reason: 0,25 = 25%, which falls between 0% (not possible) and 50% (equally likely), so the likelihood is 'less likely'.

subQuestions.questionText:
The instructions on the ready-mix plaster bag are:
• Use 7 litres of water for a 40 kg bag of ready-mix plaster.
• Mix the water and plaster for 4 minutes to achieve a good consistency.
• Do not overmix.
• Allow the mixture to stand for 3 minutes for additives to dissolve.
• Mix again for about 2 minutes.
• Plaster is ready for use.

Determine the time that Unathi must start mixing the first bag of ready-mix plaster if she wants this bag to be ready for use at 08:05.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Total mixing time: $4 + 3 + 2 = 9$ minutes ✓
Mark 2: Subtracting 9 minutes from 08:05 ✓
Mark 3: Correct start time ✓

Calculation:
Total time = $4 \text{ min (mix)} + 3 \text{ min (stand)} + 2 \text{ min (mix)} = 9$ minutes
Start time = $08:05 - 9 \text{ min} = 07:56$

Answer: $07:56$

subQuestions.questionText: Calculate (rounded to TWO decimal places) how many gallons of water she will use to mix five bags of plaster, if one gallon = 3,78541 ℓ. (One bag uses 7 litres of water.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Total litres needed: $5 \times 7 = 35$ ℓ ✓
Mark 2: Conversion: $35 \div 3,78541$ ✓
Mark 3: Correct answer rounded to 2 decimal places ✓

Calculation:
Total water = $5 \times 7 = 35$ ℓ
Gallons = $35 \div 3,78541 = 9,2466...$
         $\approx 9,25$ gallons

Answer: $9,25$ gallons

subQuestions.questionText:
The plaster reaches its full strength 21 days after it has been applied, at an average room temperature of 73,4 °F. Convert this temperature to °C.

You may use the following formula: $°F − 32° = (1,8 \times °C)$
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Substitution: $73,4 - 32 = 1,8 \times °C$ ✓
Mark 2: Calculating left side: $41,4 = 1,8 \times °C$ ✓
Mark 3: Dividing both sides by 1,8: $°C = 41,4 \div 1,8$ ✓
Mark 4: Final answer with unit: $23$ °C ✓

Calculation:
$°F - 32° = 1,8 \times °C$
$73,4 - 32 = 1,8 \times °C$
$41,4 = 1,8 \times °C$
$°C = 41,4 \div 1,8$
$°C = 23$

Answer: $23$ °C

subQuestions.questionText: The owners plan to build a cylindrical pool with diameter = 7 m and depth = 1 m. Give ONE reason why you think the cylindrical pool is designed for small children.

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the meaning of capacity of a swimming pool.
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Reference to the amount of liquid/water ✓
Mark 2: Reference to maximum holding amount ✓

Answer: The capacity of a swimming pool is the maximum amount of water (liquid) that the pool can hold when it is full. It is usually measured in litres or cubic metres.

[Accept any answer that correctly describes capacity as the volume of water a pool can hold, measured in litres/$m^3$/kilolitres.]

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate, rounded to the nearest litre, the difference in volume of the two swimming pools.

Cylindrical pool: Diameter = 7 m, Depth = 1 m
Rectangular pool: Length = 6,2 m, Width = 3,25 m, Depth = 1,65 m

NOTE: $1 \text{ m}^3 = 1\,000$ litres

You may use the following formulae:
Volume of a cylinder = $3,142 \times (\text{radius})^2 \times \text{depth}$
Volume of a rectangular prism = $\text{length} \times \text{width} \times \text{depth}$
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Radius of cylinder: $7 \div 2 = 3,5$ m ✓
Mark 2: Volume of cylinder: $3,142 \times (3,5)^2 \times 1$ ✓
Mark 3: Volume of cylinder = $38,4895$ $m^3$ ✓
Mark 4: Volume of rectangular pool: $6,2 \times 3,25 \times 1,65$ ✓
Mark 5: Volume of rectangular pool = $33,2475$ $m^3$ ✓
Mark 6: Difference: $38,4895 - 33,2475 = 5,242$ $m^3$ ✓
Mark 7: Conversion to litres: $5,242 \times 1\,000 = 5\,242$ litres ✓
Mark 8: Rounded answer with unit ✓

Calculation:
Cylindrical pool: radius = $7 \div 2 = 3,5$ m
Volume = $3,142 \times 3,5^2 \times 1 = 3,142 \times 12,25 \times 1 = 38,4895$ $m^3$

Rectangular pool:
Volume = $6,2 \times 3,25 \times 1,65 = 33,2475$ $m^3$

Difference = $38,4895 - 33,2475 = 5,242$ $m^3$
In litres: $5,242 \times 1\,000 = 5\,242$ litres

Answer: $5\,242$ litres (cylindrical pool has the larger volume)

subQuestions.label: 4.2.4(a)

Mark 1: Valid reason ✓

Acceptable answers (any ONE):

[Any reasonable answer relating to breakage, wastage, or future replacement is accepted.]

subQuestions.label: 4.2.4(b)
subQuestions.questionText:
Tiles are 20 cm × 20 cm with 16 in a box. The tiler states that he requires more than 100 boxes of tiles to complete the tiling. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether his statement is valid.

You may use the following formula: Surface area of an open cylinder = $3,142 \times \text{radius} \times (\text{radius} + 2 \times \text{depth})$
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Radius = $3,5$ m ✓
Mark 2: Substitution: $3,142 \times 3,5 \times (3,5 + 2 \times 1)$ ✓
Mark 3: Inner bracket: $(3,5 + 2) = 5,5$ ✓
Mark 4: Surface area = $3,142 \times 3,5 \times 5,5 = 60,4835$ $m^2$ ✓
Mark 5: Converting to $cm^2$: $60,4835 \times 10\,000 = 604\,835$ $cm^2$ ✓
Mark 6: Adding 10% extra: $604\,835 \times 1,1 = 665\,318,5$ $cm^2$ ✓
Mark 7: Area of one tile: $20 \times 20 = 400$ $cm^2$ ✓
Mark 8: Number of tiles needed: $665\,318,5 \div 400 = 1\,663,3$ ≈ 1664 tiles ✓
Mark 9: Number of boxes: $1\,664 \div 16 = 104$ boxes ✓
Mark 10: Comparing 104 with 100 ✓
Mark 11: Conclusion: statement is VALID ✓

Calculation:
Radius = $7 \div 2 = 3,5$ m
Surface area = $3,142 \times 3,5 \times (3,5 + 2 \times 1)$
             = $3,142 \times 3,5 \times 5,5$
             = $60,4835$ $m^2$
Convert to $cm^2$: $60,4835 \times 10\,000 = 604\,835$ $cm^2$
With 10% extra: $604\,835 \times 1,1 = 665\,318,5$ $cm^2$
Area of one tile: $20 \times 20 = 400$ $cm^2$
Tiles required: $665\,318,5 \div 400 = 1\,663,3 \approx 1\,664$ tiles
Boxes required: $1\,664 \div 16 = 104$ boxes

Conclusion: $104 > 100$, so the tiler's statement that he requires MORE THAN 100 boxes is VALID. ✓

subQuestions.questionText: It is 16 km from Himeville to Mkomazana. The distance between Mkomazana and the hotel is 4,4 km. Calculate how many kilometres after the split in the road the hotel (indicated with *H on the map) is located.
subQuestions.memoText:

subQuestions.questionText: Mkomazana offers 2-sleeper and 6-sleeper accommodation options. (Lanri, Neo and three friends = 5 people total.) Name, with a reason, the cottage you would recommend for the group to book.

subQuestions.questionText: Neo states that the total cost for the accommodation will be R8 100 if they stay in the cottage from Thursday to Saturday night. Verify, showing ALL calculations, whether his statement is VALID. (6-sleeper midweek rate = R2 640; 6-sleeper weekend rate = R2 730 per night.)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Identifying nights: Thursday (midweek), Friday (weekend), Saturday (weekend) ✓
Mark 2: Midweek cost (Thursday): $1 \times R2\,640 = R2\,640$ ✓
Mark 3: Weekend cost (Friday + Saturday): $2 \times R2\,730 = R5\,460$ ✓
Mark 4: Total cost: $R2\,640 + R5\,460 = R8\,100$ ✓
Mark 5: Conclusion that statement is VALID ✓

Calculation:
Thursday night = midweek rate = R2 640
Friday night = weekend rate = R2 730
Saturday night = weekend rate = R2 730

Total = R2 640 + R2 730 + R2 730
      = R2 640 + R5 460
      = R8 100

Conclusion: The total is exactly R8 100, so Neo's statement is VALID. ✓

subQuestions.memoText:

Mark 2: Substitution: $588 \div 7$ ✓
Mark 3: Final answer with unit: $84$ km/h ✓

      = $588 \div 7$
      = $84$ km/h

subQuestions.questionText:
The accommodation, petrol and tollgate fees for the round trip to Mkomazana will be shared equally amongst all group members. Calculate the total cost per person.

Fuel consumption: 6,42 ℓ/100 km
Fuel price: R21,40 per litre
Tollgate fees (one-way): T₁ De Hoek R56,00; T₂ Wilge R77,00; T₃ Tugela R82,00; T₄ Mooi R58,00; T₅ Marianhill R13,50
Distance one-way: 588 km
Group: 5 people (Lanri, Neo and 3 friends)
Accommodation: R8 100 (from Q5.2.3)
subQuestions.memoText:
Mark 1: Round trip distance: $588 \times 2 = 1\,176$ km ✓
Mark 2: Total fuel needed: $\dfrac{1\,176}{100} \times 6,42 = 75,4992$ ℓ ✓
Mark 3: Petrol cost: $75,4992 \times R21,40 = R1\,615,68$ ✓
Mark 4: Total tollgate fees one-way: $56 + 77 + 82 + 58 + 13,50 = R286,50$ ✓
Mark 5: Total tollgate fees round trip: $286,50 \times 2 = R573,00$ ✓
Mark 6: Accommodation cost: $R8\,100$ ✓
Mark 7: Total cost: $R8\,100 + R1\,615,68 + R573,00 = R10\,288,68$ ✓
Mark 8: Dividing by group size: $R10\,288,68 \div 5$ ✓
Mark 9: Final cost per person: $R2\,057,74$ (or $R2\,057,73$) ✓

Calculation:

Step 1: Round trip distance
$588 \times 2 = 1\,176$ km

Step 2: Petrol cost
Fuel needed = $\dfrac{1\,176}{100} \times 6,42 = 75,4992$ ℓ
Petrol cost = $75,4992 \times R21,40 = R1\,615,68$

Step 3: Tollgate fees (round trip)
One-way total = $R56 + R77 + R82 + R58 + R13,50 = R286,50$
Round trip = $R286,50 \times 2 = R573,00$

Step 4: Accommodation
$R8\,100$ (from Q5.2.3)

Step 5: Total cost
$R8\,100 + R1\,615,68 + R573,00 = R10\,288,68$

Step 6: Cost per person
$R10\,288,68 \div 5 = R2\,057,74$

Answer: $R2\,057,74$ per person (approximately R2 057,73 – R2 057,74 depending on rounding).
